hints: Separate the differential equation as \(\frac{dy}{y-1}=\frac{dx}{(x+1)(x+3)}\) before integrating.
Decompose the x-side into \(\frac{A}{x+1}+\frac{B}{x+3}\), determine \(A\) and \(B\), and integrate both sides logarithmically.
Combine the logarithms, use \(x=0,y=2\) to determine the constant, then exponentiate and isolate \(y\); the condition fixes the appropriate sign.
walkthrough:
Separate variables by dividing by $(y - 1)$ and multiplying by $dx$:
$$\dfrac{1}{y - 1}\,dy = \dfrac{1}{(x + 1)(x + 3)}\,dx$$

Express the rational function on the right-hand side in partial fractions:
$$\dfrac{1}{(x + 1)(x + 3)} \equiv \dfrac{A}{x + 1} + \dfrac{B}{x + 3}$$

Clear denominators to form the polynomial identity:
$$1 \equiv A(x + 3) + B(x + 1)$$

Write the separated equation with the partial fractions:
$$\int \dfrac{1}{y - 1}\,dy = \int \left( \dfrac{1/2}{x + 1} - \dfrac{1/2}{x + 3} \right)\,dx$$

Use the initial condition $y = 2$ when $x = 0$ to find the constant $c$:
$$\ln|2 - 1| = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln|0 + 1| - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln|0 + 3| + c$$
$$\ln(1) = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(1) - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(3) + c$$
$$0 = 0 - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(3) + c \implies c = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(3)$$

Factor out $\dfrac{1}{2}$ on the right-hand side and apply logarithm laws $\ln a + \ln c - \ln b = \ln\left(\dfrac{ac}{b}\right)$:
$$\ln(y - 1) = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \ln(x + 1) - \ln(x + 3) + \ln(3) \right)$$
$$\ln(y - 1) = \dfrac{1}{2} \ln\left( \dfrac{3(x + 1)}{x + 3} \right) = \ln\left( \sqrt{\dfrac{3x + 3}{x + 3}} \right)$$

Exponentiate both sides to solve for $(y - 1)$:
$$y - 1 = \sqrt{\dfrac{3x + 3}{x + 3}}$$

Add $1$ to isolate $y$ explicitly in terms of $x$:
$$y = 1 + \sqrt{\dfrac{3x + 3}{x + 3}}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Separable Differential Equations: Separates variables and integrates the separated equation. Derives term \(\ln(y-1)\). The final result is \(\displaystyle y=1+\sqrt{\frac{3x+3}{x+3}}\), or equivalent.
